what_this_is: The Workshop rows for asking a small model a declared question and trusting the answer only after it got known cases right: asking, routing to an owner, scoring the models on offer, keeping that calibration, measuring a confidence line, adding a wrong verdict as a known case, recognising a repeat, and answering typed questions about a state. Rubrics, owners, models and keys are the person's own; the tool carries none.

payload.label: Ask a small model a question about some text, and trust it only if it got my known cases right (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Ask a small model one question about some text (yes or no, which of a list, or how much on a scale) and get its answer with how sure it is, but only after that model got my already-answered cases right
payload.description: Give rubric (your question, answer_shape {kind: true-or-false | one-of with options | score with levels, and for a score score_tolerance: how many levels away still counts as right}, calibration cases [{content, expect}] with at least two different answers, optional confidence_bands [{at_least, then}], accept_when_answer_in) or rubrics_file plus rubric_id, the content, and providers (the models you can ask: {via: locally-served, endpoint} for a model server on your computer, or {via: hosted-classifier, endpoint, model, key_file} for a hosted classifier whose key is in a file you name). A rubric with no cases, or whose cases all expect the same answer, is refused, and so is a model that gets a case wrong, so a yes-man never becomes your judge. Returns the answer, accepted (does your rubric accept it), confidence, the whole spread, the band your rubric drew for that confidence, who answered and the scoreboard of who was tried. Content longer than a provider row's accepts_characters is refused, never cut; a row that declares no limit is sent the whole content, so declare one for any model with a smaller reading window. remember_file keeps the calibration so later questions are one call; log_file (with excerpt_characters, how much text to keep) keeps each verdict with an excerpt so a wrong one can be turned into a known case with tool:tell-it-when-it-was-wrong.

rubric.description: The question, its answer_shape, its calibration cases and accept_when_answer_in

rubrics_file.description: A file {providers?, rubrics: [...]} on your computer, instead of rubric

content.description: The text the question is about

content_parts.description: Extra addressed parts of the content, for models that read them

providers.description: The models you can ask, in the order to try them. A row is {via: locally-served, endpoint, timeout_seconds} or {via: hosted-classifier, endpoint, model, samples, key_file or needs_no_key}; every one of those fields is required, none has a default. Optional on either: accepts_characters (the most text that model reads), calibration_timeout_seconds, label

passes.description: How many times each calibration case is asked (default 2)

sure_at.description: Report whether confidence is at least this

remember_file.description: Where to keep what calibration settled

calibrate.description: false: only read the kept calibration, never calibrate now

log_file.description: A file to append each verdict to, with an excerpt of the text; needs excerpt_characters

excerpt_characters.description: With log_file: how many characters of the text to keep in the log (enough to recognise it later, not a transcript)

get_it: run npm install in the checkout (BLAKE3, which keys what calibration settled)
needs: a model server on your computer (for example Ollama) or a hosted classifier with its key in a file
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Tell the person the answer, how sure it was and which model gave it; if band is set, do what their rubric says that band means.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict, ported without its turn-hook, model-server launchers or engine adapter

payload.label: Pick which of my places holds the answer to what I am looking for (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Given something I am looking for and a list of places an answer could live, say which place most likely holds it, how sure that is, and which to try next
payload.description: Give looking_for (the text), owners ([{id, holds (what that place keeps), ask (how to look there), for_example: [texts that belong there]}]) providers (the models you can ask) and your three settings: pass_when_share_correct (the share of the owners' own examples a model must file back under the right owner before it is used, above 0 and at most 1; below 1 lets that share of mis-filed examples through), confidence_bands ([{at_least, then}], what to do at which confidence) and band_when_confidence_unknown (what to do when a model gives an answer with no probability). None has a default. The examples are the calibration: a model that files fewer of them back under their own owner than your share is refused, and one that meets it is used even if it mis-files a few. Returns go_to, confidence, what_to_do (the then of the band that confidence falls in), how to look there and then_try, the close seconds, so a near tie is looked at in both places. The model only chooses among the owners you listed, so its worst mistake is the second-best place to look.

pass_when_share_correct.description: The share of the owners' own examples a model must file back under the right owner

confidence_bands.description: What to do at which confidence

band_when_confidence_unknown.description: What to do when a model answers with no probability

get_it: run npm install in the checkout (BLAKE3, which keys what calibration settled)
needs: a model server on your computer (for example Ollama) or a hosted classifier with its key in a file
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Say which place to look first and how, and the next one when the band you set for that confidence says to look further.

payload.label: See which of my models can judge each of my questions (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Score every model I can ask against every question in my rubrics file and show who agrees with the answers I already know, how long it took and who did not answer
payload.description: Give rubrics_file ({providers: [...], rubrics: [...]} on your computer) and optionally passes (default 2). Every model on offer is asked every calibration case of every rubric. Returns, per rubric, one row per model: cases right out of cases asked, time, wrong answers, cases with no answer (a connection or time-limit problem, not a wrong answer) and whether it can judge that question. A model that is excellent at one job can be a coin flip at another; this is how you find out which. It changes nothing.

providers.description: Overrides the providers in the file

get_it: run npm install in the checkout (BLAKE3, which keys what calibration settled)
needs: a model server on your computer (for example Ollama) or a hosted classifier with its key in a file
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Tell the person, per question, which models can judge it and which cannot.

payload.label: Test my models on my questions ahead of time and keep who passed (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Calibrate every question in my rubrics file against the models I can ask, once and away from the moment of asking, and keep which model passed each so a later question is one fast call
payload.description: Give rubrics_file and remember_file (where to keep the result), optionally passes (default 1). Calibration is the slow part, a model call per known case, so doing it inside a quick question is cut off and starts again. Returns per rubric the model chosen and the scoreboard, or why none was (nothing passed, or nothing could be reached). A model that could not be reached is tried again next time; one that answered and was wrong, or answered too slowly, stays lost for six hours. Changing a rubric's question, cases or bar, or the set of models, calibrates again.

get_it: run npm install in the checkout (BLAKE3, which keys what calibration settled)
needs: a model server on your computer (for example Ollama) or a hosted classifier with its key in a file
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Tell the person which questions are ready and, for any that are not, the reason given.

payload.label: Measure where my confidence line belongs instead of guessing a round number (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Work out, from my rubric's known cases, how sure a model has to be before I act, by measuring how sure it is on known-true and known-false cases
payload.description: Give rubrics_file, optionally rubric_id (one rubric) and band (the name of the confidence band whose at_least is the line, to show where it is now). A model that passes the rubric is asked every case and its confidence on the cases it got right is kept by label; the line goes where the two groups separate, ties to the higher line. If true and false cases overlap it says so and does not lower the line to make a check talk; if the cases are one-sided it asks for cases that expect the opposite answer. Needs a model that returns a probability (a hosted classifier); a model that only writes text has no confidence to measure.

get_it: run npm install in the checkout (BLAKE3, which keys what calibration settled)
needs: a hosted classifier with its key in a file, or a model server that gives probabilities
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Tell the person the measured line, how many cases fall on the wrong side, and whether it is a clean split.

payload.label: Fit a pass line and a fail line for a model's yes or no, from lines I already ruled on (runs on your computer)
payload.job: From a model's scores on lines I already ruled good or bad, work out where it should pass a line, where it should fail one, and whether its question can tell my good lines from my bad ones at all
payload.description: Give bad and good: for each line the person ruled bad or good, the model's probability of the failing answer (a number, a list with one per sentence whose highest counts, or null for no answer). t_fail is set so at most fail_good_share_at_most of good lines fail; t_pass so at most pass_bad_share_at_most of bad lines pass, never above t_fail; scores between are uncertain. The answer gives AUC, recall at t_fail and the share of good lines failed, or failed or left uncertain, each held out (leave one out), and says usable only when every bar in usable_when holds (auc_at_least, bad_lines_at_least, recall_at_least, good_failed_or_uncertain_at_most); otherwise unseparable with the reasons. It asks no model: the scores come from the caller, on lines the model was never trained on.

get_it: run npm install in the checkout (BLAKE3, which the shared core imports)
needs: the model's probability of the failing answer on lines the person ruled good or bad
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. The bars are the person's: ask them, never invent them. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Tell the person the two lines, the held-out shares and, when it is unseparable, each reason; an unseparable question needs better lines or a better question, not looser bars.

provenance.source: Written for the Trillion film tools: a decider's two thresholds and usability fitted from a person's ruled lines

payload.label: Tell a judge it was wrong, so it is tested on that case from now on (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn a verdict that was wrong into a known case in my rubrics file, so every model is tested against it from the next calibration on
payload.description: Give rubrics_file, rubric_id, should_have_been (true, false, a number or one of the options), and either about (the text) or log_file (a verdict log written by tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict, the last verdict for that rubric is used), and optionally because. Adds one labelled case and stops: it does not change the question, the line or the model. The same text twice is not added twice (a different label corrects the earlier one). Adding cases makes a rubric harder to pass, which is the point: a model that cannot handle the new case stops being chosen for the question.

should_have_been.description: The answer it should have given

about.description: The text the wrong verdict was about

log_file.description: A verdict log to take the text from

because.description: Why the first answer was wrong

It edits the person's rubrics file; say so, and that calibration runs again.

payload.label: Count how often the same kind of thing has been flagged, even in different words (runs on your computer)
payload.job: When something is flagged again, file it under the earlier flag it repeats, or as a new kind, and say how many times and in how many sessions it has come up
payload.description: Give memory_file (where the flagged shapes are kept), rubric_id (which question it was flagged under), excerpt (the flagged text), keep_characters (how much of a new flagged text to store) and optionally session and providers. Once an earlier flag exists you also give plainly_the_same_at (the word overlap, above 0 and at most 1, at which two texts are the same without asking anyone); with providers you also give pass_when_share_correct (the share of the earlier flags a model must file back under themselves before it is trusted) and same_at_least (the confidence at which a model's pick counts as the same kind). None has a default. The same kind in different words is a closed choice over the earlier flags put to a small model, which cannot invent a kind that is not on the list; at most 40 earlier flags, each shown as its first 300 characters, are offered in one question, because that is what fits a small model's reading window. With no providers only text at or above your overlap is a repeat, so shapes are overcounted rather than a repeat count inflated. Returns the shape, times, sessions, first_seen and repeat. The count, not louder wording, is what to tell the person.

keep_characters.description: How many characters of a new flagged text to store

plainly_the_same_at.description: Word overlap at which two texts are the same without asking a model; needed once an earlier flag exists

pass_when_share_correct.description: With providers: the share of earlier flags a model must file back under themselves

same_at_least.description: With providers: the confidence at which a model's pick counts as the same kind

payload.label: Answer several typed questions about one thing in one request (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Ask a model several questions about one piece of state at once and get one answer for each, in the type I asked for, or a refusal if any is missing or the wrong type
payload.description: Give state (any JSON), questions ({<id>: {type: choice | score | noul, instructions, criteria?}}: choice answers with one of the names in criteria, or any text without criteria; score answers with a number; noul is yes or no answered as the likelihood of yes, 0 to 1), endpoint (a model server on your computer), model and timeout_seconds (no default). The state and the questions are written into the prompt and the answer schema names every question id, so the reply cannot use keys of its own. Returns answers keyed by question id. A server that answers with an error status, is unreachable or too slow, or sends a body that is not JSON, and a model reply that is not JSON, leaves a question out, or answers one in the wrong type, are each refused with a sentence saying which, rather than repaired. A noul answer is the likelihood of yes, a number from 0 to 1, checked as such (the old package accepted any text for it). This is an uncalibrated read of the state; for a decision, use tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict.

endpoint.description: Where the model server is, for example the address Ollama listens on

timeout_seconds.description: How many seconds the model server may take; a value that is not a number above zero is refused

needs: a model server on your computer (for example Ollama) with a chat model
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request to a file, run `run` with that file as {input}, and read the last line: { result } or { error } saying what to change. Report each answer under its question.

payload.label: Answer the yes or no questions my checks ask, with a small model on my computer (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Answer the questions a check of my writing asks a model, one line at a time, with the small model, adapter or hosted model each of my check rows names, keeping every answer so a line is never asked twice
payload.description: Give settings_record (record:setting:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, the person's setting row, read through tools/settings) and asks, the questions tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts lists: each { question, options, text } with the row's adapter ({ name, blake3 }: decider-2b with that LoRA adapter, its folder the setting's adapters[name], checked by BLAKE3 before loading), model ({ mlx: repo id } a downloaded MLX chat model at its one snapshot, { consult: name } a hosted model through the consult-model route, or { stand_in } fixed answers), examples ({ items: <set>, bad_for }: the person's ruled lines of that set, rows of list:checks with kind labelled-line, shown first and never the judged line) and context (where the line sits in its film). mode live asks a model for what the answer cache lacks; cache answers only from it. Answers one { option: probability } or null per ask, in order.

asks.question: Is this line vague?
asks.text: The kettle boils in two minutes.

provenance.source: Moved from the launch-video copy gate's decider layer (decider_layer.py answer), its model, cache and adapter paths made the person's settings

payload.label: Measure whether a small model can answer my check's question, on lines I already ruled on (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Ask a small model my check rows' questions about every line I already ruled good or bad, and fit where each row should pass and fail a line, and whether it is usable at all
payload.description: Give settings_record (the person's setting row for this tool, read through tools/settings: its fit bars, good_sets, frame and models), rules (ids of the person's check rows with an ask, record:check:<id>) and lines (the set of labelled lines, rows of list:checks with kind labelled-line and that set). Ruled lines (each with good) count by their own ruling, optionally only one split and only those with context (context_only); lines kept by set count as good when a set the setting's good_sets names holds them. Each line is asked one question a sentence and scored by its worst sentence, then tool:fit-pass-and-fail-lines fits t_fail, t_pass, AUC, recall and the held-out shares with the setting's bars (fpr overrides fail_good_share_at_most). Answers { <rule id>: finding }; the person writes a finding into that row's ask.calibration. Lines a model was trained on must never calibrate it.

provenance.source: Moved from the launch-video copy gate's decider layer (decider_layer.py calibrate), its labelled lines and bars made the person's rows and settings
